name: ARIA dutasteride trials
question: Does dutasteride improve symptoms and reduce acute urinary retention and BPH surgery compared with placebo in men with symptomatic enlarged prostates?

design.blinding: double-blind after a single-blind placebo lead-in
design.population: Men at least 50 years old with clinical BPH, AUA Symptom Index at least 12, Qmax at most 15 mL/s, prostate volume at least 30 cm3, and PSA 1.5–10 ng/mL; postvoid residual greater than 250 mL, AUR within 3 months, prior prostate surgery, alpha-blocker use within 4 weeks, and any prior 5-alpha-reductase inhibitor use were excluded.
design.locator: Full text, Materials and Methods, p 435; Debruyne 2004 PubMed abstract, Objectives

verdictNote: The 48-month comparison was open-label; both groups received dutasteride after month 24.
takeaway: Across three randomized ARIA trials, dutasteride versus placebo improved 24-month AUA symptom score (−4.5 versus −2.3 points) and reduced acute urinary retention (39/2,167 versus 90/2,158); BPH surgery was less frequent (47/2,167 versus 89/2,158). Peak flow improved more with dutasteride in men with symptomatic enlarged prostates.

results.measure: Mean change from original baseline at month 48, open-label ITT
results.note: Between-group comparison at month 48; both groups also improved from month 24 (p<0.001 each). No confidence interval reported. Open-label ITT denominators are enrollment counts, not month-48 measurement counts.

results.measure: Mean Qmax change from original baseline at month 48, open-label ITT
results.note: Between-group comparison at month 48; D/D improved from month 24 (p=0.007) and P/D improved after switching (p<0.001). No confidence interval reported.

results.measure: Mean percentage change from original baseline at month 48, open-label ITT
results.note: Between-group comparison at month 48. From month 24 to 48, TPV decreased in P/D (p<0.001), but the further D/D decrease did not reach significance (p=0.07). No confidence interval reported.

results.endpoint: Acute urinary retention and BPH-related surgery
results.measure: Crude incidence through month 48, double-blind ITT denominators; both groups received dutasteride after month 24
results.note: AUR and surgery caused study withdrawal; the 48-month figures retain original double-blind ITT denominators. The paper reports percentages without event counts or confidence intervals.
results.locator: Full text, Materials and methods, p 490; Table 4, p 493
